siblings.analysis: Storage-disjoint: confirmed (A-then-B and B-then-A both succeed on anvil). NOT economically disjoint: A's tx5 opens StableStakerV2.claim, turning ~205.42 AM pending (32 staker/pool pairs) into mintable raw AM while Antimatter.totalSupply()==0 and no AM market exists. Any claimer can then createPair(AM,sUSDS) and/or seed it at an arbitrary ratio; B's step-0 R1 guard then aborts permanently. Demonstrated: claim (25.4768 AM) -> createPair -> B preview exit 1 with the exact R1 abort string. createPair needs no AM, so R1 griefing pre-exists; A-first adds an organic (non-griefer) actor class with motive (a holder wanting to trade AM) and the ability to set the initial price.
No interaction with A's state beyond shared OWNER nonce/balance. After A+B the OWNER still holds 0.004899 ETH on the fork for C.

operational.resumeCorrectness: Gates are chain-state and byte-exact (routes compared by keccak of path/swapParams/pools; pool key exact; claimEnabled read). Partially-set routes cannot exist (each setRoute is one atomic tx). Resume with a different-nonce address: progress address = local-pass prediction; if a different contract sits there (e.g. B's seeder if both scripts raced on one nonce) _checkImmutables reverts (poolManager() missing) -> safe abort. No-code address -> abort with delete instruction. Verified by story fork tests (resume, no-code abort) on 26303500.
